articles.title: NASA Revamps Challenge Linking Community College Studies to Aerospace Careers
articles.summary: Community college students across the U.S. now have another opportunity to discover how their education can lead to fulfilling roles at the forefront of aerospace, science, engineering, and technology. articles.content:
Community college students across the U.S. now have another opportunity to discover how their education can lead to fulfilling roles at the forefront of aerospace, science, engineering, and technology. The updated NASA Community College Aerospace Scholars (NCAS) student challenge invites students to learn about the agency and its missions, engage with NASA experts, and explore aerospace jobs while competing for monetary awards.

The applications period is currently open. The deadline to register is Monday, Sept. 28.

“What makes this opportunity unique is that it’s one of few that is specifically for community college students,” said Alicia Baturoni Cortez, project manager for NASA’s Minority University Research and Education Project, which administers NCAS. “The NCAS student challenge is designed to meet their needs and broaden their career awareness so they can either go right into the workforce or expand their goals to include a four-year degree in STEM.”

A launch pad for new possibilities

Kim Alexander, left, and Ashley Rodriguez pose for a photo at NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland on their first day as interns in January 2024. NASA/Erik Lopez

For NASA interns Kim Alexander and Ashley Rodriguez, NCAS became an unexpected springboard from community college to new careers.

After eight years as a bartender, Alexander was looking for a way to launch her career. She enrolled at Riverside Community College in Riverside, California, originally intending to pursue graphic design – but fell in love with math instead. Alexander participated in NCAS hoping it would look good on her resume and university transfer application. She ended up on a winning team that designed a human mission to Mars. The experience influenced her entire career trajectory.

“I was just completely overwhelmed by how amazing the program was,” said Alexander, who went on to participate in other NASA student opportunities. “But NCAS was the most monumental, because I really started thinking, ‘Hey, I could pursue a career in this. This is feasible.’”

Rodriguez grew up in South Florida, where she watched space shuttle launches but never considered a career at NASA. Instead, she gained experience in various roles and was parenting a toddler by the time she went back to school at Miami-Dade Community College seeking an IT degree. That’s where she first heard about NCAS, which ultimately set her on a path to a career in strategic communications.

“I did an infographic on laser relay communications. I knew nothing about it, then I felt like a pro by the end.” Ashley Rodriguez NASA Intern

The experience showed her the importance of strategic communications at NASA and helped her to discover a field she enjoys.

In January 2024, Rodriguez and Alexander started NCAS-funded NASA internships in the agency’s Aerosciences Evaluation and Test Capabilities Portfolio Office, where they met their mentor, Data and Analytics Manager Erik Lopez.

Today, both have earned university degrees and are starting NASA Pathways internships that could lead directly to full-time NASA employment. Rodriguez is working as a strategic communications intern in the Engineering Performance Management Office at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida, while Alexander is beginning an engineering role supporting the Flight Demonstrations and Capabilities Project at the agency’s Armstrong Flight Research Center in Edwards, California.

“They were the first two NCAS alumni interns; they literally onboarded together,” Lopez said. “And the fact that they now both get to come back to the agency as Pathways interns just brings me so much joy.”

NCAS relaunches with updated mission, prize potential

Stories like Alexander’s and Rodriguez’s illustrate the impact NCAS can have, and underscore why the program’s updated mission aims to reach even more community college students.

This school year, NCAS is launching with a two-part mission. The cohort phase, which runs through fall, calls on students to participate in live virtual experiences with NASA experts and submit materials detailing a connection between their current coursework and a role at NASA. Faculty members are key to encouraging students who might not envision themselves in a NASA role. Up to 1,000 submissions will be eligible for a $500 award.

Those who successfully complete this phase will be invited to take part in the next phase, a spring virtual NCAS career fair linking them to experts and industry career opportunities. Upon completion of the career fair, students may submit additional materials for prizes of $250, for up to 500 of the top submissions.

“What NCAS does is bring the stars down to ground level. It allows students a risk-free exploration of what could be.” Alicia Baturoni Cortez Project Manager, NASA’s Minority University Research and Education Project

To explore NCAS timelines and eligibility requirements and take your education to the next level, visit: https://nasa-ncas.org/student-overview/.

articles.personality_title: NASA expands program to connect community college students with aerospace careers
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Many community college students want to explore careers in science and technology but often lack clear paths to jobs in fields like aerospace. NASA’s Community College Aerospace Scholars (NCAS) program helps fill this gap by offering learning and career opportunities.

**What happened** – NASA updated the NCAS challenge, inviting community college students across the U.S. to participate in virtual activities, connect with NASA experts, and compete for cash awards. The program’s application deadline is September 28. Students who complete the first phase can join a spring career fair and compete for additional prizes.

**Impact** – The program is unique because it focuses specifically on community college students, many of whom may not have considered aerospace careers. Examples include Kim Alexander and Ashley Rodriguez, who started at community colleges and through NCAS gained internships at NASA, leading to university degrees and promising careers. This shows how NCAS can open doors to STEM fields for students with diverse backgrounds.

**What's next step** – This school year, NCAS will continue offering virtual events and career fairs to reach more students. NASA hopes the program grows, encouraging more community college students to see STEM careers as achievable and helping them gain valuable experience and connections.

**One-sentence takeaway** – NASA’s updated NCAS program offers community college students a clear path to explore and build careers in aerospace through learning, mentorship, and internships.
articles.personality_title_fr: La NASA élargit un programme pour relier les étudiants des collèges communautaires aux carrières aérospatiales
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – De nombreux étudiants des collèges communautaires souhaitent découvrir des carrières en science et technologie, mais manquent souvent de parcours clairs vers des emplois dans des domaines comme l’aérospatiale. Le programme Community College Aerospace Scholars (NCAS) de la NASA aide à combler ce vide en offrant des opportunités d’apprentissage et de carrière.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – La NASA a mis à jour le défi NCAS, invitant les étudiants des collèges communautaires à travers les États-Unis à participer à des activités virtuelles, à se connecter avec des experts de la NASA et à concourir pour des prix en argent. La date limite d’inscription est le 28 septembre. Les étudiants qui terminent la première phase peuvent participer à une foire de l’emploi au printemps et concourir pour d’autres prix.

**Impact** – Le programme est unique car il cible spécifiquement les étudiants des collèges communautaires, beaucoup n’ayant pas envisagé de carrières dans l’aérospatiale. Par exemple, Kim Alexander et Ashley Rodriguez, qui ont commencé dans des collèges communautaires et, grâce au NCAS, ont obtenu des stages à la NASA, menant à des diplômes universitaires et des carrières prometteuses. Cela montre comment le NCAS peut ouvrir des portes aux domaines STEM pour des étudiants aux parcours variés.

**Prochaine étape** – Cette année scolaire, le NCAS continuera d’offrir des événements virtuels et des foires de l’emploi pour toucher plus d’étudiants. La NASA espère que le programme se développera, encourageant davantage d’étudiants des collèges communautaires à voir les carrières STEM comme accessibles et à acquérir de l’expérience et des contacts précieux.

**Résumé en une phrase** – Le programme NCAS mis à jour par la NASA offre aux étudiants des collèges communautaires un chemin clair pour explorer et construire des carrières dans l’aérospatiale grâce à l’apprentissage, au mentorat et aux stages.
articles.personality_title_es: La NASA amplía programa para conectar a estudiantes de colegios comunitarios con carreras aeroespaciales
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Muchos estudiantes de colegios comunitarios quieren explorar carreras en ciencia y tecnología, pero a menudo no tienen caminos claros hacia empleos en campos como la aeroespacial. El programa Community College Aerospace Scholars (NCAS) de la NASA ayuda a cubrir esta necesidad ofreciendo oportunidades de aprendizaje y carrera.

**Qué pasó** – La NASA actualizó el desafío NCAS, invitando a estudiantes de colegios comunitarios de todo Estados Unidos a participar en actividades virtuales, conectarse con expertos de la NASA y competir por premios en dinero. La fecha límite para inscribirse es el 28 de septiembre. Los estudiantes que completen la primera fase pueden unirse a una feria de carreras en primavera y competir por premios adicionales.

**Impacto** – El programa es único porque se enfoca específicamente en estudiantes de colegios comunitarios, muchos de los cuales no habían considerado carreras aeroespaciales. Por ejemplo, Kim Alexander y Ashley Rodriguez comenzaron en colegios comunitarios y, gracias a NCAS, obtuvieron pasantías en la NASA, logrando títulos universitarios y carreras prometedoras. Esto muestra cómo NCAS puede abrir puertas en campos STEM para estudiantes con diferentes antecedentes.

**Próximo paso** – Este año escolar, NCAS continuará ofreciendo eventos virtuales y ferias de empleo para llegar a más estudiantes. La NASA espera que el programa crezca, animando a más estudiantes de colegios comunitarios a ver las carreras STEM como alcanzables y ayudándoles a obtener experiencia y contactos valiosos.

**Conclusión en una frase** – El programa actualizado NCAS de la NASA ofrece a los estudiantes de colegios comunitarios un camino claro para explorar y construir carreras en aeroespacial mediante aprendizaje, mentoría y pasantías.
